treaty_name: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of India and the Government of the Kingdom of Belgium for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income (1993, with Protocol 1993, as modified by Notification SO 54(E) of 2001; modified by MLI)
eif_quote: Whereas the annexed Agreement between the Government of the Republic of India and the Government of the Kingdom of Belgium ... has come into force on the first day of October, 1997, the thirtieth day after the receipt of later of notifications by both the Contracting States to each other of the completion of the procedures required for bringing into force of the said Agreement ... Notification : No. GSR 632(E), dated 31-10-1997, as amended by Notification No. SO 54(E), dated 19-1-2001.
source_title: Income Tax Department (India), India-Belgium DTAA with Notifications GSR 632(E)/1997 and SO 54(E)/2001 (Wayback copy of official incometaxindia.gov.in page, captured 2017-07-02)

rates.quote: 2. However, such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends, is a resident and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the dividends is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

2. However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State the tax so charged shall not exceed :— ( a ) 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest, if such interest is paid on any loan of whatever kind granted by a bank; and ( b ) 15 per cent of the gross amount of the interest in all other cases.

"2. However, such royalties and fees for technical services may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the royalties or fees for technical services is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties or fees for technical services."

ppt.quote: 1. Notwithstanding any provisions of a Covered Tax Agreement, a benefit under the Covered Tax Agreement shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Covered Tax Agreement.

notes: Effective dates (Art. 29(1)): Belgium, tax due at source on income credited or payable on or after 1 January 1998; India, previous years beginning on or after 1 April 1998. Royalty/FTS cap of 10% results from the MFN clause in para. 1 of the 1993 Protocol (royalties and fees for technical services only), triggered by the India-Sweden Convention and implemented by official Indian Notification SO 54(E) dated 19-1-2001 with effect from 1 April 1998 in India and 1 January 1998 in Belgium (it also narrowed the royalty definition in Art. 12(3)(a)). The original Art. 12(2) cap was higher (superseded). No MFN for dividends or interest. Not modelled: Art. 11(2)(a) 10% cap for interest on loans granted by a bank (recipient-type condition). Protocol signed 2017-03-09 (reported in force 2025-06-26, not verified in an official gazette): per the Belgian Chamber bill 55K2016/001 (dekamer.be) it replaces Art. 26 (exchange of information) and Art. 27 (assistance in collection) only - no change to Arts. 10-12. MLI: covered by both; MLI WHT provisions effective 2020-01-01 on the Belgian side; India chose Art. 35(2) 'taxable period', so on the Indian side from 1 April 2020. India chose the Simplified LOB (Art. 7(6)) but Belgium's MLI deposit position contains no SLOB choice and no Art. 7(7) acceptance, so only the PPT applies.
unverified: Entry into force of the 2017 Protocol (reported 2025-06-26) not verified in an official source; it does not affect Arts. 10-12
Indian-side MLI date 2020-04-01 derived from India's Art. 35(2) choice
